title: Rotational Motion & Torque
summary: Rotation mirrors linear motion with angular position, velocity, and acceleration. Torque $\tau=rF\sin\theta$ is the turning effect of a force; $\tau=I\alpha$ is the rotational $F=ma$; and angular momentum $L=I\omega$ is conserved without external torque.

lever arm.plain: Perpendicular distance from axis to force.

concept_sections.heading: Angular quantities
concept_sections.explanation: Rotation uses angular position, velocity $\omega$, and acceleration $\alpha$, linked to linear motion by $v=r\omega$ and $a=r\alpha$.

concept_sections.heading: Torque
concept_sections.explanation: Torque is the turning effect of a force: $\tau=rF\sin\theta$. It's largest with a long lever arm and a perpendicular push.
math_steps: Find the distance from the axis.
Maximum when the force is perpendicular.

concept_sections.heading: Moment of inertia and $\tau=I\alpha$
concept_sections.explanation: Moment of inertia is rotational mass; the net torque gives angular acceleration via $\tau=I\alpha$.

concept_sections.heading: Rotational equilibrium and energy
concept_sections.explanation: For balance, net torque is zero; a spinning object stores $\tfrac12I\omega^2$ of energy.

concept_sections.heading: Angular momentum conservation
concept_sections.explanation: With no external torque, $L=I\omega$ stays constant; drawing mass inward lowers $I$ and speeds up rotation.

real_world_examples.title: A wrench on a bolt
real_world_examples.scenario: A longer wrench loosens a stubborn bolt.
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: The longer lever arm increases torque for the same force.

real_world_examples.title: A diver's tuck
real_world_examples.scenario: A diver tucks to flip faster.
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: Reducing $I$ raises $\omega$ since angular momentum is conserved.

real_world_examples.title: A merry-go-round
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: Torque changes its spin; angular momentum accounts for the new rate.
